image_description: A male mallard duck (drake) standing on a sandy or dirt ground. The duck features the characteristic iridescent green head, white neck ring, grey/brown body plumage, and yellow bill. It is captured in a walking posture with one orange webbed foot visible.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Most distinctive feature is the broad, flat bill adapted for filter-feeding; bill is dark grey to yellow-green.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The bill is clearly visible, broad, flat, and yellowish-green, matching the description perfectly.
The eye is visible and appears dark/black, consistent with the taxonomy.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Body is stocky and compact, streamlined and buoyant with dense waterproof plumage.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The body shape is robust and streamlined. The plumage texture appears dense and smooth, indicative of waterproof feathers.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Breeding plumage is typically more colorful than female: common patterns include iridescent green head with white neck ring and grey body (mallard), or chestnut head with grey body.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image shows the classic Mallard drake pattern: iridescent green head, distinct white neck ring, and grey/brown body.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Legs are short and set far back on the body with webbed feet (three forward toes connected by webbing).
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: One leg is clearly visible. It is orange, short, and ends in a webbed foot. The anatomy looks biologically correct.
The folded wing is visible on the side, showing proper layering and structure. While not 'spread', the visible portion is consistent with broad, pointed wings.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Tail is short with curled central tail feathers (drake feathers) in many species.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The tail is visible at the rear. The characteristic upward curl of the central tail feathers (speculum area/curled feathers) is present.

selected_experts.reason: To confirm the specific species identification (Mallard Drake) and rule out hybrid or misclassified bird types.
To verify the structural integrity of the legs and feet, ensuring no fusion or missing digits in the webbed foot.
To check for edge bleeding between the fine feathers of the neck ring and the background, and ensure the bill connects cleanly to the head.
To assess the texture realism of the feathers and the lighting consistency on the iridescent head.

focus_areas: Boundary sharpness of the white neck ring
Iridescence rendering on the green head
custom_prompts_for_reflector: Pay close attention to the transition between the white neck ring and the green head/chest. AI often blurs this boundary. Also, inspect the visible foot for any 'melting' into the ground or incorrect toe count.
